craft_notes: Sthāyin: outer and inner both needed. Rows: still-outer yet inner-veils. Read aloud: balanced rule.

lines: Truly for the then-entered, still outer is to be done, to cut off the bound —
and who too thus shares not the sinking —
his chief is the outer rite;
since for him too, but the beast-veiling inner rite,
when mounted thereon, of his thought-force is purity-giving.
l4.sanskrit_cite: satyataḥ tadāviṣṭasya tathāpi bahir api kāryo yāgo 'vacchedahānaya eva yo 'pi tathā samāveśabhāk na bhavati tasya mukhyo bahiryāgaḥ tadabhyāsāt samāveśalābho yatas tasyāpi tu paśutātirodhānāyāntaryāgaḥ tadarūḍhāv api tatsaṃkalpabalasya śuddhipradatvāt
